source_caption:
Dimple Kapadia initially thought the audition call for movie "TENET" was a prank, wondering why would Christopher Nolan, arguably the most obsessive filmmaker alive want her? In fact, she was so nervous she tried to recommend other actors for the part instead. Nolan, however, refused to take no for an answer he flew to Mumbai specifically to meet her, even holding the camera himself during her screen test. This scene is the result of that persistence: a masterclass in "Quiet Aura" where she holds the screen against John David Washington with effortless, cold authority.

Tenet remains one of the most confusing films of all time  yet also one of Christopher Nolan’s most once-in-a-lifetime achievements. Very few filmmakers would even attempt something this structurally insane. With its renowned for its groundbreaking use of "time inversion," allowing characters and objects to move backward through time while the world moves forward, creating a unique,, high-concept espionage thriller.

source_details.title: Tenet
source_details.synopsis: Tenet (stylized in all caps, previously as TENƎꓕ) is a 2020 science fiction action film written and directed by Christopher Nolan, who also produced it with his wife, Emma Thomas. It stars John David Washington, Robert Pattinson, Elizabeth Debicki, Dimple Kapadia, Michael Caine, and Kenneth Branagh. The film follows a CIA officer who is recruited into a secret organization, tasked with tracing the origin of objects that are traveling backward through time and their connection to an attack by the future. Nolan took over five years to write the screenplay after deliberating about Tenet's central ideas for more than a decade. Pre-production began in late 2018, casting took place in March 2019,
